messages:
Lin (support): Heads up — after the 10:02 deploy we're getting a sharp uptick in 502/504 from hosted inference API. Customer tickets piling, some timeouts too. :rotating_light:
Maya (sre): Noted. Can you paste the sample request + time window?
Lin (support): 10:05-10:20 PST. Example curl from prod repros 502 quickly:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-xl\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response headers show `502 Bad Gateway` and sometimes `504` after ~15s.
Ravi (runtime): deploy-bot shows a config toggle flip during the canary: `enable_precise_batching=true` for canary and `false` for stable. That flag touched batching window logic.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T10:02:11Z started by @ravi (cookie: 0a9f), canary target=10% -> 100% in 30m.
Maya (sre): metrics-bot — can you post 5xx rate & latency for /v1/generate grouped by route?
metrics-bot: dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/requests?route=/v1/generate&since=2026-03-17T09:55Z — canary slice shows 14% 5xx, stable 0.6%. Median p99 tail latency jumped from 120ms -> 3.2s on canary.
Jo (oncall): I attempted a manual rollback of the canary at 10:12 but traffic slice didn't shrink to 0 immediately — some routers still sticky. Rolling back again now.
Ravi (runtime): That flag touched the batching path that interacts with route-level timeout. If batching waits for size and the route timeout isn't extended it can hit proxy drain and return 502. The change increased batch wait from 10ms -> 500ms in the implementation.
Lin (support): Customers reporting billing anomalies too — some requests show no token charge and returned 502. Is that expected?
Maya (sre): Not expected. 502s should not bill; looks like billing system either saw requests upstream before the failure or logs are delayed. We'll open a billing ticket after stabilization. Focus on service first.
Ravi (runtime): Patch idea — revert `enable_precise_batching` or set `batch_max_wait_ms=20` in the canary config. Need a coordinated rollback to avoid split-brain of flags across routers.
Jo (oncall): I'm coordinating with infra to force roll back the config selector across regions, running `orchestrator rollback --id 0a9f --force`. ETA 2m.
Maya (sre): In parallel, add a short-circuit to the route to bypass batching for requests with `x-debug: true` so support can repro unique traces.
Lin (support): I'll share repro steps and a failing request ID after we get the bypass. Also sharing a failing trace ID: trace-20260317-abc123.
Ravi (runtime): Found log snippet from one failing worker:
```
2026-03-17T10:07:33Z ERROR handler.go:289 request_id=trace-20260317-abc123 err=\"upstream timeout waiting for batch\" pool=serve-core canary=true
```
Jo (oncall): Rollback completed at 10:14; routers cleared sticky cookies at 10:16. Early telemetry shows 5xx dropping to baseline by 10:18.
metrics-bot: post-rollback snapshot: canary 5xx -> 0.9%, p99 latency back to 140ms.
Maya (sre): Root cause: misapplied batching flag increased wait window and interacted poorly with route timeouts during canary. Action items:
- Ravi: push a safe default `batch_max_wait_ms=20` and add a canary-stage test for route timeout interactions.
- Jo: verify global selector propagation and add a guard in orchestrator to prevent partial flag state longer than 30s.
- Lin: compile customer-facing incident note with ETA and affected customers, note billing follow-up.
Ravi (runtime): Agreed. Also adding telemetry to emit `batch_wait_ms` per request for 24h.
Lin (support): I'll send the incident update to customers now, marking mitigated. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
